metadata.title: Periodization
metadata.purpose: Defines how TRAIN programs are structured over time — how weeks build on each other, when to push, when to deload, and how to progress from phase to phase. This is the architecture that turns a collection of workouts into a real training system.

instructions_for_claude.step_1: Identify client goal and experience level — these determine which periodization model to use
instructions_for_claude.step_2: Select the appropriate model: Linear (beginner), Undulating (intermediate), or Block (advanced/performance)
instructions_for_claude.step_3: Map client's available weeks to the correct mesocycle template below
instructions_for_claude.step_4: Assign weekly focus (accumulation, intensification, realization, deload) using the week_by_week_structure
instructions_for_claude.step_5: Apply volume and intensity progressions from programming_variables.json within each week
instructions_for_claude.step_6: Set deload week — default week 4 of every mesocycle
instructions_for_claude.step_7: Define what the next mesocycle looks like at the end — TRAIN programs never just stop, they transition

mesocycle.definition: A training block of 4–8 weeks with a specific focus — the primary unit of TRAIN programming
mesocycle.extended_length: 6 weeks (4 weeks accumulation + 1 week intensification + 1 week deload) — intermediate and advanced
mesocycle.coaching_note: Every client program is built in mesocycles. A client asking for an '8-week program' is asking for 2 mesocycles. Always think in blocks, not individual weeks.

macrocycle.definition: The full training year or multi-month plan — made up of multiple mesocycles
macrocycle.standard_for_train: 3–6 month macrocycle (2–4 mesocycles) — appropriate for most clients
macrocycle.coaching_note: Most TRAIN clients won't need macrocycle planning initially. Focus on delivering the first mesocycle excellently, then transition into the next.

microcycle.definition: A single training week — the smallest repeating unit
microcycle.coaching_note: Each week within a mesocycle has a specific intensity and volume target. Weeks are not interchangeable — they build on each other.

supercompensation.definition: The physiological process by which the body adapts to training stress and comes back stronger — only occurs during recovery, not during training itself
supercompensation.implication: Training causes fatigue. Rest and deload cause adaptation. Both are required. A client who never rests never fully adapts.
supercompensation.coaching_language: The gains happen when you rest — not when you lift. The training is just the signal. Your body does the real work between sessions.

fatigue_fitness_relationship.definition: Both fitness and fatigue accumulate during training. Fitness persists longer than fatigue. Deloading removes fatigue and reveals the fitness underneath.
fatigue_fitness_relationship.practical_application: A client who feels flat or stale before their deload week will often feel significantly stronger and more capable in week 5 (first week of next mesocycle). This is the system working correctly.
fatigue_fitness_relationship.coaching_language: If you're feeling a little tired going into deload week — that's exactly right. That means the training did its job. Week 5 is going to feel like a different body.

linear_periodization.description: Volume starts moderate and decreases over the mesocycle. Intensity starts moderate and increases over the mesocycle. Simple, predictable, effective for anyone new to structured training.
linear_periodization.principle: One variable changes at a time — load increases as reps decrease. Easy to understand, easy to track.

week_1.purpose: Learn the program, establish movement patterns, build work capacity

week_2.purpose: Add volume, increase load slightly, build on week 1 foundation

week_3.purpose: Peak training stress — this is the hardest week, drive adaptation

week_4.purpose: Remove fatigue, allow supercompensation, prepare for next mesocycle

load_progression_example.week_5_new_mesocycle: Squat 3x12 at 110 lbs (start next block above week 1 baseline)

linear_periodization.coaching_note: Linear periodization is the most powerful tool for beginners because they respond to almost any progressive stimulus. Don't overcomplicate it — consistent load increases week over week is all that's needed.

undulating_periodization.description: Volume and intensity vary within the week — different sessions have different rep ranges and focuses. More stimuli = more adaptation pathways = continued progress when linear has stalled.

daily_undulating.name: DUP — Daily Undulating Periodization
daily_undulating.description: Each session in the week has a different rep range and intensity focus

example_upper_lower_week.monday_upper: Strength focus — 4x5-6, heavy load, long rest
example_upper_lower_week.tuesday_lower: Hypertrophy focus — 4x8-12, moderate load, moderate rest
example_upper_lower_week.thursday_upper: Endurance/Volume focus — 3x15-20, light-moderate load, short rest
example_upper_lower_week.friday_lower: Hypertrophy focus — 4x8-12, moderate load, moderate rest

daily_undulating.advantage: Each muscle group experiences multiple rep ranges per week — maximizes both strength and hypertrophy adaptations

weekly_undulating.name: WUP — Weekly Undulating Periodization
weekly_undulating.description: Each week of the mesocycle has a different focus — week rotates between strength, hypertrophy, and volume
weekly_undulating.advantage: Simpler to manage than DUP — good transition from linear for intermediate clients

mesocycle_structure.weeks_1_to_2: Establish the undulating pattern — clients need 2 weeks to adapt to the variable stimulus
mesocycle_structure.weeks_3_to_4: Push each session's intensity to its target range
mesocycle_structure.weeks_5_to_6: Intensification — hit the higher end of each rep range with heavier loads
mesocycle_structure.week_6_or_7: Deload — full recovery before next mesocycle

undulating_periodization.coaching_note: DUP is the most evidence-supported periodization model for simultaneous strength and hypertrophy development. It feels more complex initially but clients quickly adapt to the variety. The different stimuli each session is what breaks plateaus.

block_periodization.description: Training is organized into sequential specialized blocks — each block has one primary focus. Accumulation (volume) → Intensification (strength) → Realization (peaking) → Deload. Not used for beginners.

accumulation_block.focus: Volume — build work capacity and muscle
accumulation_block.goal: Build the foundation of volume that intensification and realization will be built on

intensification_block.goal: Convert volume adaptations into strength — heavier weights, fewer reps

realization_block.focus: Peak — express maximum strength and performance
realization_block.goal: Test strength, compete, or set PRs — remove fatigue while maintaining intensity

deload_transition.focus: Full recovery before next macrocycle or mesocycle
deload_transition.purpose: Remove all accumulated fatigue before the next training block begins

block_periodization.coaching_note: Block periodization is powerful but requires advanced clients who can tolerate high volume in the accumulation block. Do not apply to beginners or general health clients — linear or undulating will serve them better.

mesocycle_templates.description: Ready-to-use mesocycle structures for each goal. Claude fills in the exercises from the exercise libraries.

week_2_accumulation.session_density: Higher — introduce supersets on accessory work

week_3_intensification.session_density: High — supersets on most accessory and finisher work

week_4_deload.session_density: Low — straight sets only, no supersets
week_4_deload.cardio_addition: 2x20 min easy walking or light cardio only

fat_loss_4_week.mesocycle_2_adjustment: Increase week 1 baseline above previous week 1. Add one additional superset per session. Increase cardio by 5-10 min per session.

week_1_foundation.purpose: Establish mind-muscle connection with new program

week_2_accumulation.purpose: Increase load slightly — same rep range, heavier weight

week_4_deload.purpose: Full recovery — reduce load by 40%, maintain movement patterns

muscle_gain_4_week.mesocycle_2_adjustment: Introduce weekly undulating periodization — rotate hypertrophy, strength, and volume weeks. Add 1 set per primary exercise across the board.

weeks_1_to_3_accumulation.explosive_work: Include 2-3 power exercises per session at session start

weeks_4_to_6_intensification.explosive_work: Increase explosive work intensity — box jumps, medicine ball, sprint work

weeks_7_peak.focus: Express strength — test PRs or competition performance

general_health_4_week.philosophy: Consistency is the goal. Every week should feel challenging but doable. The client should finish each session feeling accomplished, not destroyed.

week_1.note: Ease in — form and confidence first

week_2.note: Add one set to primary movements

week_3.note: Slight increase in load and density

week_by_week_coaching.description: What TRAIN communicates to the client each week — grounded in Kim's voice and the periodization phase

week_1.client_expectation: This week may feel easier than expected. That's intentional. We're building the foundation, not burning it down on day one.
week_1.coach_focus: Movement quality, mind-muscle connection, program familiarity
week_1.kim_language: Week one isn't about going hard — it's about going smart. Learn the program this week. Feel every movement. We're building something real here.

week_2.client_expectation: Things will start to feel more challenging. You'll notice muscle soreness earlier in the week.
week_2.coach_focus: Confirm progression — are RPEs climbing appropriately? Adjust if needed.
week_2.kim_language: You should be feeling it now. That's your body adapting. Keep showing up exactly like you did this week — the work is accumulating even when you can't see it yet.

week_3.client_expectation: This is the hardest week of the mesocycle. Fatigue will be higher. Performance may feel slightly off near the end of the week — that's normal.
week_3.coach_focus: Watch for form breakdown under fatigue. Monitor recovery signals.
week_3.kim_language: Week three is where it gets real. You're going to have to dig a little deeper this week — and you can. This is what you've been building toward. One more push, then we recover.

week_4.client_expectation: Sessions will feel significantly easier. Some clients feel restless or like they're 'not doing enough.' That feeling is the system working.
week_4.coach_focus: Hold the client to the deload — do not let them add volume or intensity.
week_4.kim_language: I know this week feels light. It's supposed to. The gains happen in recovery — not in the gym. Your body is doing more this week than it did in week three. Trust the process. Week five is going to feel incredible.

week_5_new_mesocycle.client_expectation: Most clients feel noticeably stronger and more capable at the start of a new mesocycle. This is supercompensation — it's real and it's earned.
week_5_new_mesocycle.coach_focus: Set new baseline above previous mesocycle week 1. Acknowledge the progress.
week_5_new_mesocycle.kim_language: Feel that? That's what we've been building. Your new starting point is above where you were 5 weeks ago. That's progress you can feel. Now let's build again.

plateau_management.definition: When progress stalls — performance doesn't improve week over week for 2+ consecutive weeks despite consistent training and recovery
assessment_checklist: Is the client actually tracking and progressing load week over week?
Is sleep quality sufficient? (Poor sleep = stalled recovery = stalled progress)
Is stress chronically high? (High cortisol impairs adaptation)
Is nutrition adequate? (Extreme deficit + high volume = plateau)
Has the client been on the same program for more than 8 weeks? (Neural adaptation — needs new stimulus)
Is the client training near failure consistently, or coasting at RPE 6?

solutions.deload_and_reset: If client has been pushing hard for 6+ weeks without a deload — insert an immediate deload week before progressing
solutions.change_rep_range: Shift to a different rep range for 4 weeks — if on hypertrophy (8-12), shift to strength (4-6) then return
solutions.change_exercise_variation: Swap primary movement for a variation — barbell squat → Bulgarian split squat, barbell bench → dumbbell press
solutions.add_volume: If RPE has been consistently under 7 — add 1 set per primary exercise
solutions.address_recovery: If sleep or stress are the issue — reduce volume, prioritize recovery, address root cause first
solutions.change_periodization_model: If on linear for 2+ mesocycles — transition to undulating. More stimulus variety breaks adaptation plateaus.

plateau_management.coaching_language: Plateaus are not failures — they're feedback. Your body has adapted to the current stimulus and is asking for something different. This is actually a sign of progress. Let's look at what the data is telling us and adjust.

transition_between_mesocycles.description: How TRAIN programs the bridge from one mesocycle to the next — programs never just end

rules.new_baseline: Week 1 of mesocycle 2 always starts above week 1 of mesocycle 1 — this is the proof of progress
rules.keep_what_works: Exercises that drove the most progress stay in the program. Exercises that felt neutral rotate out.
rules.introduce_variation: Swap 1-2 exercises per session to provide new stimulus without completely changing the program
rules.increase_complexity: If client has mastered all movements — introduce more complex variations or periodization models
rules.reassess_goal: At each mesocycle transition, check in on goal alignment — has the client's goal evolved?

beginner.mesocycle_2: Linear 4-week — same split, heavier baseline, 1-2 new exercise variations
beginner.mesocycle_3: Linear or intro to weekly undulating — introduce split if ready

intermediate.mesocycle_1: Linear or weekly undulating — establish new baseline
intermediate.mesocycle_2: Undulating (DUP or WUP) — increase stimulus variety

advanced.mesocycle_3: Block — realization + transition to next macrocycle

periodization_by_life_context.description: Real clients have real lives. Periodization must adapt to context — not just physiology.

high_stress_period.trigger: Client reports very high stress, major life event, illness
high_stress_period.adjustment: Insert an extra deload week or reduce volume by 30% for 1-2 weeks. Do not push accumulation during life stress.
high_stress_period.coaching_language: Life is part of training. When life gets heavy, we lighten the load in the gym — so you have energy for what matters most. We'll push again when you're ready.

travel_weeks.trigger: Client is traveling or has limited equipment access
travel_weeks.adjustment: Swap to minimal equipment program for the week. Maintain frequency — 2-3 sessions of bodyweight or hotel gym work.
travel_weeks.coaching_language: Travel doesn't stop training — it just changes the tools. We're keeping you consistent this week, not perfect.

holiday_and_social_events.trigger: Client has upcoming social events, holidays, reduced schedule
holiday_and_social_events.adjustment: Treat as deload week if timing aligns. If not — reduce to 2 sessions of full body work.
holiday_and_social_events.coaching_language: Life is meant to be lived. A week of reduced training won't erase progress — but burning out trying to maintain perfection might. Let's be smart about this.

competition_or_event_prep.trigger: Client has a specific event — race, photo shoot, wedding, competition
competition_or_event_prep.adjustment: Back-plan from event date. Insert realization phase 1-2 weeks before event. Deload the week of event.
competition_or_event_prep.coaching_language: We're building toward your date. Everything from now until then has a purpose — we're peaking you at exactly the right moment.
